land.text: the Chaldean marsh land at the head of the Gulf

successors.note: The Bit-Yakin page does not describe an annexation; Sennacherib's 694 invasion "to subjugate Elam and Chaldea" is its last event.

capitals.name: Dur-Yakin (site not on the pages)
capitals.note: "The tribal capital was Dur-Yakin, the original seat of Marduk-Baladan"; no site or coordinates on the pages, so this is a placeholder in the middle of the First Sealand core at the head of the Gulf.

correction.text: the marsh land at the head of the Gulf, "the territory that once made the Sealand", the Chaldean core

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -852..-695: no Cliopatria shape. The page says the extent "is not known precisely" but "ran from the lower Tigris into the Arabian Peninsula" (Sargon II places it as far as Dilmun); Marduk-apla-iddina II's page: the tribe was "originally established in the territory that once made the Sealand in southern Babylonia". Drawn as the First Sealand core (8,320 km2: the marsh and Gulf head), a reading well short of the page's maximal description.

region.text: the Chaldean marsh land at the head of the Gulf

ledger.note: 852 BC (bridged): the Chaldean tribes first appear. "The very first written historical attestation of the existence of Chaldeans occurs in 852 BC" in Shalmaneser III's annals; the Bit-Yakin page says Bit-Yakin is not named in that entry and gives no founding of the tribal state. The start is the first notice of the Chaldeans, not of Bit-Yakin.

694 BC (bridged): Sennacherib invades Chaldea. After Nergal-ushezib's coup in 694 "Sennacherib responded by invading to "subjugate Elam and Chaldea" and sacking Babylon"; the page describes no annexation and ends the tribe's history with the failed revolt of 700 "in the Chaldean tribal land of Bit-Yakin" and Marduk-apla-iddina II's death in exile. The end is the last notice of the polity. Mirrors the neo-assyrian-empire gain.

wars.name: Marduk-apla-iddina II against Sargon II
wars.outcome: The Bit-Yakin chief seized the Babylonian throne in 722 (page: "between 721 and 710"); Sargon II "eventually drove him from Babylon (c. 710 BC)" and he fled to Elam; an attempt to defeat him near Der in 720 "was unsuccessful".
wars.note: The babylonia dossier carries the throne years (-721 to -710); this war is the same fighting seen from his tribe.

wars.name: Marduk-apla-iddina II against Sennacherib
wars.outcome: In 703 he "returned from Elam", reigned nine months and was defeated near Kish; his last failed revolt was "in the Chaldean tribal land of Bit-Yakin" in 700; in 694 Sennacherib invaded to "subjugate Elam and Chaldea".
wars.note: The Marduk-apla-iddina page gives no 700 or 694 date for Bit-Yakin and dates his death "c. 697-694 BC" (infobox).

certainty.note: The extent is "not known precisely"; the shape is the marsh core only.

sources.title: Bit Yakin

notes:
SCOPE. The Chaldean tribal lands the brief names; Cliopatria lacks them (cliopatria_names empty). Only Bit-Yakin is written; Bit-Dakkuri, Bit-Amukani, Bit-Shilani and (the Chaldea page's) "Bet-Adini" are named without dates or lands and have no dossier.
PAGES. Three (Bit Yakin, Chaldea, Marduk-apla-iddina II); the Shalmaneser III page was opened (for Bit Adini) and says only that the Arabs and Chaldeans first appear in his annals from the 850s.
DATES ARE WEAK. Start -852 is the first mention of the Chaldeans (not of Bit-Yakin); end -694 is the last notice (Sennacherib's invasion), with no annexation described. Both are confidence 1. The page also gives "Eriba-Marduk, another Chaldean, succeeded him in 769 BC" (not tied to Bit-Yakin) and Nabopolassar, a Chaldean chieftain, who seized Babylon in 626 (620 on the Chaldea page): the neo-babylonian-empire dossier carries that dynasty. A Bit-Yakin of the 7th century after 694 (the Chaldean marsh and Elam) is not on the pages.
EXTENT. The pages describe Bit-Yakin as running from the lower Tigris into the Arabian Peninsula, as far as Dilmun (Sargon II); the drawn shape is the First Sealand core only. Gazetteer names missing: Dur-Yakin, Bit-Yakin, Dilmun, Kish (not used). The capital is a placeholder.
MIRROR. neo-assyrian-empire carries the gain at -694 (confidence 1).
